documents.title: Office Visit - HTN / anticoagulation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6-month follow-up.
Feels well. On warfarin 5 mg since last August; INRs here every 2-4 weeks, the clinic calls her with the plan. Had one low reading this month and has been back within her INR goal since. No bleeding, no new skin changes. No palpitations.
Shoulder fine. Knees: same morning stiffness, walks it off.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg; HCTZ 25; methimazole 10; calcium carbonate 600 TID; D3 2000. No OTC pain relievers.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear. No edema. Skin: old pigmented patches on lower abdomen/thighs, intact.
A/P: HTN - at goal on HCTZ. Graves - TSH/FT4 today. PAF on warfarin - in sinus by exam. Osteoporosis - calcium/D, walking. AWV September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV 2025.
HRA reviewed. Independent; lives alone. Mostly retired now, an occasional consulting job from home.
Falls: history of fall with fracture 9/2023; none since. TUG normal. Wears grippy shoes, uses handrail on stairs.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1 - drinks less wine than she used to, mostly none.
Cognition: no concerns.
Diet: dairy most days now, plenty of vegetables, steady for the warfarin.

Problems: HTN (HCTZ 25), Graves (methimazole 10, euthyroid), PAF on long-term warfarin (anticoag clinic), osteoporosis with 2023 humerus fragility fracture (declined drug therapy; calcium carbonate 600 TID + D3 2000), hypofibrinogenemia 7/2024, knee OA, lactose intolerance, L IOL.
Meds reconciled - no changes.

Exam: vitals as charted. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear. Kyphosis mild.

Plan:
- BMP, CBC today.
- Colonoscopy due 2026 (last 2016). We'll talk options at a spring visit; she's on warfarin now.
- Mammogram 11/2024 normal; next 11/2026.
- Flu + COVID in October.
- ACP: still hasn't signed the proxy form. Discussed again; she'll bring it to the next visit.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No ST-T abnormality. Unchanged from 07/09/2024.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Annual review of Sandra Walsh on 09/23/2025 - paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin.
No palpitations, no recurrence that she is aware of since July 2024. No bleeding, no bruising, no skin problems since the 2024 necrosis episode. INRs over the past year have mostly been between 2 and 3 on 5 mg daily, with an occasional reading just outside the range that came back on recheck.
Medications: warfarin 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; methimazole 10 mg daily; calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm.
Plan: continue warfarin 5 mg, INR goal 2-3, dosing through our anticoagulation clinic with draws at your lab. Annual follow-up.

Cardiology

documents.title: Emergency Department provider note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE - 01/10/2026

Chief complaint: confusion, constipation and weakness for two weeks.

HPI: 72-year-old woman with osteoporosis, hypertension, Graves disease and paroxysmal AF on warfarin, brought in by her sister. Over the past two weeks she has been muddled - losing track of conversations, forgetting what she went into a room for - with constipation and generalized weakness. No fever, falls, head injury, headache, vomiting or urinary symptoms.
Wanting to strengthen her bones, she has been taking extra calcium carbonate tablets she buys over the counter on top of her usual 600 mg three times a day, and drinking milk every day; she thinks this started around the fall but cannot say how many extra tablets a day. She also takes her prescribed thiazide diuretic for blood pressure.

Medications (patient and sister):
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- calcium carbonate 600 mg three times daily, plus additional OTC calcium carbonate tablets (amount unknown)
- cholecalciferol 2000 units daily
- methimazole 10 mg daily
- warfarin 5 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 88. Lethargic but rousable. No focal neurological deficit. Abdomen soft, non-tender, non-distended. No bruising or bleeding.

Labs: calcium 12.5 mg/dL (8.5-10.2); creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (0.6-1.1); BUN 35 mg/dL (7-20); serum bicarbonate elevated.
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.52, HCO3 32 mEq/L, PaCO2 42 mmHg - metabolic alkalosis.
Urinalysis normal. CBC unremarkable. INR 2.9, within her warfarin goal of 2-3.

Assessment: milk-alkali syndrome - hypercalcemia, metabolic alkalosis and reduced kidney function from heavy calcium carbonate and milk intake, with a thiazide reducing urinary calcium excretion.
Plan: IV normal saline started. Hold calcium carbonate and hydrochlorothiazide. PTH sent. Admit to medicine.

medications.reason: Milk-alkali syndrome; thiazide reduces calcium excretion

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - milk-alkali syndrome
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 01/10/2026 - Discharge 01/13/2026
Principal diagnosis: milk-alkali syndrome.

Course: admitted from the ED with two weeks of confusion, constipation and weakness after months of extra over-the-counter calcium carbonate and daily milk on top of her prescribed calcium and hydrochlorothiazide. Calcium 12.5, creatinine 2.1, BUN 35, metabolic alkalosis on blood gas. Treated with IV normal saline. Calcium carbonate and hydrochlorothiazide stopped. PTH 9 pg/mL (15-65), appropriately suppressed, supporting a non-PTH cause. Calcium and creatinine improved each day. Confusion cleared by hospital day 2 and she was back to her usual self. Bowels moving before discharge.
Discharge labs: calcium 9.9 mg/dL, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL.
Warfarin and methimazole continued throughout; INR stayed within her 2-3 warfarin goal.

Discharge medications:
- STOPPED calcium carbonate (all, including OTC)
- STOPPED hydrochlorothiazide
- CONTINUE cholecalciferol 2000 units daily
- CONTINUE methimazole 10 mg daily
- CONTINUE warfarin 5 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within a week - recheck calcium and creatinine, and blood pressure off the thiazide; an alternative antihypertensive may be needed. Avoid calcium supplements; keep milk and dairy to ordinary amounts.

documents.title: Transition of care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called after discharge 1/13 (milk-alkali syndrome). Pt answered, clear and conversational, sister with her. Thinking "back to normal." Bowels OK. Drinking water.
Med review: stopped HCTZ and ALL calcium tablets - sister cleared the extra bottles out of the cupboard. Still taking vitamin D3, methimazole, warfarin. No home BP readings yet; asked her to check a few times before Friday.
PCP visit Friday 1/16 with labs.

orders.reason: antihypertensive choice after thiazide stopped (milk-alkali syndrome)

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. ED note and discharge summary reviewed.

Admitted 1/10-1/13 with milk-alkali syndrome: calcium 12.5, creatinine 2.1, BUN 35, metabolic alkalosis, PTH suppressed at 9. She had been taking extra OTC calcium carbonate on top of her 600 mg TID plus daily milk since around the fall, while on HCTZ. Treated with saline; calcium carbonate and HCTZ stopped. Discharge calcium 9.9, creatinine 1.4.

Today: thinking is clear - she and I had a normal, detailed conversation, and she recalls the hospital stay. Bowels back to normal. Energy returning. No headache.
She was upset with herself; she had read that more calcium would make her bones stronger after the fracture.

Meds now: warfarin 5 mg (anticoag clinic); methimazole 10 mg; vitamin D3 2000 units. No calcium tablets. HCTZ stopped.

Exam: BP 148/88 off HCTZ. Weight 55 kg. Alert, oriented, fluent. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs today (resulted this afternoon): calcium 9.6, creatinine 1.1 - both continuing to improve.

A/P:
1. Milk-alkali syndrome, resolving. Stop ALL calcium tablets - prescribed and OTC. Milk and dairy fine in ordinary amounts (a serving or two a day), no more "extra for the bones." Continue vitamin D3 2000 units. Repeat BMP in a few weeks.
2. HTN, BP up off the thiazide. Not restarting HCTZ. Sent a question to her cardiologist about the best replacement given her AF and warfarin; will start something once I hear back. Home BP log in the meantime.
3. Osteoporosis: without calcium tablets she'll rely on dietary calcium. Discussed.
4. PAF on warfarin: INR drawn today for the clinic.

documents.title: Cardiology letter - antihypertensive
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for your note about Sandra Walsh. With hydrochlorothiazide stopped after her milk-alkali syndrome, I agree a thiazide should not be restarted. I would suggest lisinopril 10 mg daily as the alternative, with a basic metabolic panel (potassium and creatinine) one to two weeks after starting, given the recent rise in her creatinine. Lisinopril has no meaningful interaction with her warfarin.
Her AF has been quiet; no change to anticoagulation.

Cardiology

documents.author: PCP

F/u one month on lisinopril 10 mg.
Feels well. No cough, no dizziness. Home readings in the low 130s and 120s over 70s-80s. Thinking and energy normal. No calcium tablets; milk in coffee and a yogurt most days.
Meds: lisinopril 10 daily; warfarin 5 (clinic); methimazole 10; D3 2000.
Exam: BP 130/80. Weight 55 kg. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear. No edema.
2/6 BMP: Cr 0.9, K 4.6, Ca 9.4.

A/P:
1. HTN - controlled on lisinopril 10. Continue. BMP with her next routine labs.
2. Milk-alkali syndrome - resolved; calcium and kidney function normal.
3. Colon cancer screening: colonoscopy 2016 was normal and she's due. She would rather not do a colonoscopy on warfarin (holding it and the prep worry her). FIT is a reasonable option at average risk - kit given.
4. Proxy form: brought it in signed today; scanned to chart.
